question: What is the main goal of using tele-nursing in rural Nigerian communities?

options.A: Eliminating the need for physical nursing training schools
options.B: Bridging the gap between patients and distant healthcare services
options.C: Replacing doctors completely in remote hospitals
options.D: Selling prescription drugs directly through mobile phones

explanation: You've got this! Tele-nursing simply uses technology like phones to connect patients in remote areas with nurses, helping them get care despite long distances and travel costs. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T7#GNS113_U3_T7_h1)

question: A nurse in Lagos uses a mobile phone to check on a patient with high blood pressure in a village. What is this called?
explanation: Spot on! Using mobile phones or other tech tools to deliver nursing care and monitor patients from afar is what we call tele-nursing. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T7#GNS113_U3_T7_h1)

question: Which regulatory body oversees nursing practice and professional standards in Nigeria?

options.A: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria
options.B: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria
options.D: Federal Ministry of Information and Culture

explanation: The Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria is the statutory body responsible for regulating nursing education and practice in the country. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T7#GNS113_U3_T7_h2)

question: Why is it important to get informed consent before starting a tele-nursing session?

options.A: It guarantees that the patient will pay for the internet data used.
options.B: It ensures the patient understands the limitations and virtual nature of the care.
options.C: It legally transfers all medical liability away from the attending nurse.
options.D: It replaces the need for a physical examination under all circumstances.

explanation: Great thinking! Patients need to know what to expect from remote care—including its limits—so they can make informed choices about their treatment. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T7#GNS113_U3_T7_h2)

question: Sending a photo of a healing wound via WhatsApp for a nurse to check later is an example of what?
explanation: You're doing great! When information is sent and reviewed later without a live, real-time conversation, it's called asynchronous care (like store-and-forward). [learn more](GNS113_U3_T7#GNS113_U3_T7_h3)

question: Why do we rely so much on basic voice calls and SMS text messages for tele-nursing in Nigeria?

options.A: They work well within areas with limited internet bandwidth and infrastructure.
options.B: They require high-speed fiber-optic internet connections.
options.C: They are exclusively funded by international donor agencies.
options.D: They completely replace the need for physical hospital visits.

explanation: Makes total sense! Simple tools like calls and texts work reliably even when fast broadband internet isn't available in the area. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T7#GNS113_U3_T7_h3)

question: During which phase of the nursing process does a nurse gather patient history over the phone?
explanation: You got it! Collecting a patient's history, symptoms, and details always happens during the initial assessment phase. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T7#GNS113_U3_T7_h4)

question: What is a major challenge during the diagnosis phase of tele-nursing?

options.A: Documenting care notes in a register
options.B: Direct physical examination like palpation and auscultation
options.C: Setting health goals with the patient
options.D: Asking the patient about their current symptoms

explanation: Spot on! Virtual care makes hands-on checks difficult, so nurses have to rely heavily on what the patient and their caregivers report. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T7#GNS113_U3_T7_h4)

question: A patient calls during a virtual check-in complaining of sudden chest pain and trouble breathing. What should you do first?

options.A: Advise the patient to drink warm water and sleep
options.B: Instruct the patient to go immediately to the nearest health facility
options.C: Ask the patient to send a text message later with an update
options.D: Schedule a routine follow-up call for the following week

explanation: Safety first! Chest pain and breathing trouble are red flags that need immediate in-person emergency care, not remote management. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T7#GNS113_U3_T7_h5)

question: Why are active listening and a calm tone especially important during audio-only phone calls with patients?

options.A: Telecommunication networks automatically filter out loud noises
options.B: Visual body language cues are largely absent
options.C: Patients cannot understand medical terminology spoken quickly
options.D: Nigerian regulations require nurses to speak in a specific dialect

explanation: Brilliant! Since you can't see the patient's face or body language over a phone call, your voice tone and listening skills become your best tools to build trust and spot distress. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T7#GNS113_U3_T7_h5)

question: Which of these is a major challenge for tele-nursing in Nigeria?

options.A: Excessive availability of high-speed fiber-optic cables
options.B: Strict prohibition of mobile phones in all hospitals
options.C: An overabundance of smartphones among rural farmers
options.D: Unstable electricity supply and poor network connectivity

explanation: You nailed it. Frequent power cuts (NEPA/PHED) and weak mobile networks make reliable digital healthcare quite tricky in many areas. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T7#GNS113_U3_T7_h6)

question: What is an ethical risk when healthcare relies too heavily on smartphone apps?

options.A: Hospitals completely eliminate paper record books.
options.B: Patients receive too much accurate medical information.
options.C: Nurses are forced to work fewer hours per week.
options.D: Vulnerable populations without smartphones may experience digital exclusion.

explanation: Spot on! Relying only on advanced tech can leave behind elderly or poor patients who don't have smartphones, which affects fair access to care. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T7#GNS113_U3_T7_h6)

question: What is one great way to help patients afford calling tele-nursing helplines in Nigeria?

options.A: Charging double fees for all weekend consultations
options.B: Banning all mobile phone use for medical purposes
options.C: Requiring patients to buy expensive international calling cards
options.D: Establishing toll-free health helplines in partnership with telecom providers

explanation: Great job! Toll-free numbers ensure that lack of airtime doesn't stop a patient from getting urgent nursing advice. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T7#GNS113_U3_T7_h7)

question: Why is it important to teach digital health skills in Nigerian nursing schools?

options.A: It guarantees automatic employment in foreign countries upon graduation.
options.B: It replaces clinical practice hours with video game simulations.
options.C: It equips future nurses with the skills needed for modern tech-enabled care delivery.
options.D: It ensures nursing students never have to work in physical hospitals.

explanation: Exactly! Preparing student nurses with digital skills ensures you'll be ready to confidently handle modern telehealth tools in your career. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T7#GNS113_U3_T7_h7)
